author: OpenCV Contributors (OpenCV.org / OpenCV.ai)
count_basis: VERIFIED by enumeration: GitHub contents API listing of samples/data at ref 4.x returned 94 image files totalling 9,914,974 bytes (14 further non-image files present and ignored).
label_definitions: NO classification labels ship with this corpus. Nothing below is a category label.
VERIFIED by reading the preserved files (transcribed, not inferred):

- stereo_calib.xml: an <imagelist> pairing left01.jpg<->right01.jpg ... left14.jpg<->right04.jpg. This is ground truth establishing that the left*/right* files are STEREO PAIRS of the same calibration board, i.e. distinct samples, NOT duplicates of one another.
- calibration.yml, intrinsics.yml, left_intrinsics.yml: camera intrinsic matrices for the calibration set.
- H1to3p.xml: a 3x3 homography matrix (ground truth for the pic1->pic3 view correspondence).
- aloeGT.png: disparity ground-truth MAP for aloeL.jpg/aloeR.jpg (an image, preserved in raw_images/, not a label file).

- letter-recognition.data: 20,000 rows, each a letter label (A-Z) plus 16 numeric features (the UCI Letter Recognition dataset). Tabular feature data - it does NOT label any image in this corpus and must not be joined to one.
- data01.xml: OpenCV FileNode training data for the ml sample.
- alphabet_36.txt / alphabet_94.txt: character sets for the text samples.
consent_position: Mostly not applicable (synthetic renderings, textures, calibration boards, objects, landscapes). Two files depict identifiable real people and are EXCLUDED on consent/provenance grounds - see exclusions.
citation: OpenCV Contributors, OpenCV samples/data image corpus, Apache License 2.0, https://github.com/opencv/opencv/tree/4.x/samples/data

exclusions.reason: CONSENT / PROVENANCE. lena.jpg is the 1972 Playboy centrefold crop; the depicted person (Lena Soderberg) has publicly stated she does not want the image used, and multiple venues (IEEE, Nature journals) have retired it. lena_tmpl.jpg is a crop of the same work. messi5.jpg is a press photograph of an identifiable living individual whose underlying rights are not conveyed by the repository's Apache-2.0 code licence. All three are excluded even though the surrounding corpus is permissively licensed.

notes: APPROVED. Apache-2.0 licence text fetched and verified from the repository at ref 4.x. Permits reproduction, modification and redistribution with attribution, and grants an express patent licence - so academic research and ML training are both permitted. CAUTION carried as a condition: Apache-2.0 s.6 grants NO trademark licence, so the logo files (LinuxLogo.jpg, WindowsLogo.jpg, opencv-logo.png, opencv-logo-white.png) may be analysed locally but must not be used in a way that implies endorsement or be redistributed as branding assets.
annotation_notes: Directory scan of samples/data. Companion ground-truth and calibration files (homography XML, stereo calibration XML/YAML, camera intrinsics, the letter-recognition labelled dataset) are preserved verbatim; .avi video companions are catalogued but not collected into an image dataset.

author: Jeffrey 'Alex' Clark and Pillow contributors; originally Secret Labs AB / Fredrik Lundh
count_basis: VERIFIED by enumeration: recursive GitHub git-trees API listing of ref main returned 735 image blobs under Tests/images/ totalling 23,172,855 bytes (tree not truncated).
label_definitions: NO classification labels ship with this corpus. Nothing below is a category label.
VERIFIED by reading the preserved files (transcribed, not inferred):

- Tests/images/bmp/README.txt states verbatim: 'These images are from the bmpsuite: https://github.com/jsummers/bmpsuite and are in the public domain according to the readme in the project.' THIRD-PARTY PROVENANCE: the bmp/ subset originates from Jason Summers' bmpsuite and is asserted to be public domain by that upstream project. Attribution should cite bmpsuite alongside Pillow for those files.

- Tests/images/tga/common/readme.txt documents a STRUCTURED NAMING CONVENTION: {width}x{height}_{mode}_{origin}_{compression}.tga where mode is a PIL mode in lower case, origin is 'bl' (bottom-left) or 'tl' (top-left), and compression is 'raw' or 'rle'. Filenames in that directory are therefore parseable metadata - a real, non-invented source of attributes. Images created with GIMP.
consent_position: Corpus is synthetic/technical test imagery (gradients, patterns, format edge cases, encoder fixtures). Scanned for person/sensitive filename tokens; no matches.
citation: Pillow contributors, Pillow test image corpus, MIT-CMU License, https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/tree/main/Tests/images
notes: APPROVED. MIT-CMU licence text fetched and verified. Permissive: use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense and sell all permitted with the copyright notice retained. This corpus is deliberately included as the image-quality-assessment stress test: it contains a large number of genuinely malformed, truncated and out-of-specification files produced by real-world encoders, which exercises the corruption and unsupported-format detectors against authentic failures rather than synthetic ones. Files that Pillow itself cannot decode are expected to land in rejected_images/corrupt/ - that is a correct result, not a pipeline fault.
annotation_notes: Explicit file allow-list, NOT a directory scan. This corpus ships no labels; the only provenance documentation it contains is these two README files. Scanning the repository root previously pulled in CI configuration (codecov.yml, readthedocs.yml) which is build metadata, not annotation, and has been removed.
